Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:10:2.hebrew: ודפנא - ענפי עץ ערמונים, שקורין לו"ר, ופרי שלו קורין ביי"ש:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:10:2.english: And laurel - Branches of a chestnut tree, which they call *lor* (laurel), and its fruit they call *bais* (berries).

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:11:1.hebrew: פשיטא - דהאבנים של שניהם, דאפי' לא פסק לן דינא דמתני' המלמדנו שמתחלה בין שניהם עשאוה על כרחם, היו חולקין בשוה האבנים, שהרי ברשות שניהם מונחים, ויד מי מהם תגבר:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:11:1.english: It is obvious - That the stones belong to both of them. For even if the law of the Mishnah had not ruled for us — [the Mishnah] which teaches us that at the outset they built it between them [and that either could compel the other] against his will — they would divide the stones equally, since they are lying in the domain of both, and whose hand would prevail over the other's?

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:11:2.hebrew: (הג"ה בפי' ר"ח - קמ"ל דלא בעינן ראיה, אלא שותף מפיק מיניה בלא ראיה, ואיהו דטעין דדיליה נינהו, עליו הראיה. וכל כה"ג הכי דיינינן ליה. וזה הדין מפורש עוד כמו כן בפרק הבית והעלייה בתחילתו: איבעית אימא בשותפין, כי האי גוונא אנוחי אבנים ברשות חבירו לא קפדי, וחזקת רשות לאו כלום הוא. שמעינן מינה דכל כהאי גוונא, דמילתא דידיעא בשותפתא לתרוייהו, אע"ג דמנחי ברשותא דחד מינייהו, לא יכול למיטען "דידי נינהו, דברשותי מנחי", דקי"ל שותפין לא קפדי אהדדי. ע"כ):
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:11:2.english: (Gloss: In the commentary of Rabbeinu Chananel - [the Mishnah] teaches us that we do not require proof; rather, a partner can remove it from him without proof, and he who claims that they are his, the burden of proof is upon him. And in every such case we rule this way. This law is also explained elsewhere, at the beginning of the chapter "HaBayit VeHaAliyah": "If you wish, say [that it refers] to partners. In a case like this, [people] are not particular about [a partner] placing stones in a fellow's domain, and a presumptive claim of ownership based on [use of] the domain is nothing." We learn from this that in any such case, where the matter is known to be shared by both of them, even though [the stones] are placed in the domain of one of them, he cannot claim, "They are mine, for I placed them in my domain," because we hold that partners are not particular with one another. End of quote.):

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:13:1.hebrew: השתא סתם גינה אמרת לא - אע"פ שהיזק ראיה קשה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:13:1.english: Now, [regarding] an unspecified garden, you said [that one is] not [required to build a wall]? - Even though the damage of sight is severe.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:14:1.hebrew: אמר אביי כו' - האי מקום שנהגו לגדור דקתני מתני' אבקעה קאי:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:14:1.english: Abaye said, etc. - This [clause] "a place where they were accustomed to build a fence," which the Mishnah teaches, refers to a field.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:14:2.hebrew: א"כ מאי אבל בבקעה - הא מינה סליק, והכי איבעי למיתני: אבל מקום שנהגו שלא לגדור, אין מחייבין אותו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:14:2.english: If so, what is [the meaning of] "but in a valley"? - This is already derived from it. And this is how it should have taught: "But [in a place] where they were accustomed not to build a fence, we do not compel him."

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:15:1.hebrew: מכפייה לקרנא לבר - ראשי הכותל יכוף לצד חבירו, וכל חזית לשון קצה הוא. וכן שנינו בתמיד (פ"ב מ"ד) גבי מערכה: וחזיתה מזרחה — ראשי הגזירין. וכן מחזה מול מחזה דמלכים (א ז) — ראשי הנסרים מוסבין זה מול זה. ועבי' מאבראי — כופה לצדי ראשי הכותל שמחבר בראשו אבנים וטיט ומעבהו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:15:1.english: Bending the corner outward - He bends the ends of the wall toward his neighbor's side. And every chazit is an expression for an edge. So we learned in Tamid (2:4) regarding the altar pile: "And its chazit faces east" — [meaning] the ends of the logs. Likewise, "machazeh opposite machazeh" in Kings (I 7) — [meaning] the ends of the planks are turned toward one another. And "its thickness on the outside" — he bends [it] to the sides of the ends of the wall, by joining stones and mortar at its end and thickening it.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:15:2.hebrew: דידי ודידיה הוא - כדקתני מתניתין: כשעושין אותו בין שניהם, עושין חזית מכאן ומכאן:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:15:2.english: It is both mine and his - As the Mishnah teaches: when they make it between the two of them, they make a [privacy] partition on this side and on that side.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:15:3.hebrew: השתא נמי גייז לה - לההיא כפופה שהיא לצדו. ואימא דידי ודידיה הוא, ולא עשינו חזית:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:15:3.english: Now too, he cuts it off - that bent [beam] which is at his side. And [the other party can] say: it is [a beam] of mine and of his [jointly], and we did not make a [dividing] wall.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:16:1.hebrew: מלגיו - לצד שלו. ולקמיה פריך: הא מבחוץ קתני:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:16:1.english: From within - On his own side. And later [the Gemara] raises an objection: But [the Mishnah] teaches [that it is] from the outside.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:16:2.english: He attaches it - He joins another wall [lit. front] alongside it.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:1:1.hebrew: אהדר ליה כלילא דיילי - האנקה מתרגמינן ילא (ויקרא יא), והוא שרץ שקורין הרצו"ן, ושערו קשה כמחטין, ועשה לו עטרה מעורו סביבות עיניו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:1:1.english: I will return to him a crown of yaylei - The anakah (ferret/gecko) we translate [in Aramaic] as yela (Leviticus 11). It is a creeping creature that is called herizon (hedgehog) [in French], whose hair is hard like needles. And he made for himself a crown from its skin around his eyes.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:2:1.english: Now, at any rate, [that I and you] - I and you, the two of us, are here, and there is no one listening.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:3:1.hebrew: הנני מחלל את מקדשי - סיפיה דקרא: מחמד עיניכם:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:3:1.english: Behold, I will profane My Sanctuary - The end of the verse [reads]: "the delight of your eyes."

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:4:1.hebrew: מסתפינא ממלכותא - כפופים היו למלכות רומיים:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:4:1.english: I am afraid of the government - They were subject to the Roman kingdom.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:4:3.hebrew: אי זיינך עלך ספרך כאן - אם נתגאית בכלי מלחמתך שהרגת בית אדוניך, ספר יוחסין שלך בידינו הוא, [ידענו] שאתה עבד:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:4:3.english: If your weapon is upon you, your book is here - If you have grown proud of your instruments of war, with which you killed the house of your master, [know that] your book of genealogy is in our hands; [we know] that you are a slave.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:4:4.english: Not a king, etc. - Neither a king nor the son of a king:

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:4:5.english: It becomes a free man [lit. "kalania" is made] - He becomes free on his own:

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:6:1.english: Shisha - Green marble, which is called "bayish".

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:6:2.english: And with marble - Which is white.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:6:3.english: Kuchla (blue-painted stone) - Marble that is colored like blue [kachol].

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:6:4.hebrew: אידוותא דימא - גלי הים, שהם נעים ונדים והעין מתעששת בראייתן:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:6:4.english: The waves of the sea - The waves of the sea, which move and sway, and the eye grows weak from looking at them.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:7:1.english: Daniel was punished - Further on, [the Gemara] explains his punishment.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:7:2.english: My king, let my counsel be pleasing to you - May my advice be good in your eyes:

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:7:3.english: In the bestowing of favor on the poor - In showing graciousness to the poor.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:7:4.english: Thus there will be a lengthening of your tranquility - [There will be a length] of your well-being.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:7:5.hebrew: כולא מטא - כל החלום של פורענות בא עליו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:7:5.english: All of it came [upon him] - The entire dream of calamity came upon him.

Rashi on Bava Batra 4a:7:6.english: At the end of twelve months - Because of Daniel's advice, [God] postponed [the punishment] for him for twelve months.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 4a:14:1.hebrew: הכי קתני וכן בגינה סתם כו' - וסיפא נמי יש לפרש כן: אבל סתם בקעה, ומקום שלא נהגו לגדור בגינה — אין מחייבין אותו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 4a:14:1.english: "This is what it teaches: And similarly, an unspecified garden..." etc. - And the latter clause [of the Mishnah] can also be explained in this way: But [in the case of] an unspecified field, and a place where they were not accustomed to build a fence around a garden — they do not compel him.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 4a:16:1.hebrew: והא מבחוץ קתני, קשיא - ותיובתא אינה, דמצינן למימר: היינו שבולט חוץ לחומה. מ"מ קשיא היא, דא"כ "מחוץ" הוה ליה למיתני:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 4a:16:1.english: "But it teaches 'from the outside'" – this is difficult - It is not a conclusive refutation, for we could say that this means that it projects outside the wall. Nevertheless, it is difficult, for if so, it should have taught "mi-chutz" ["from outside"]:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 4a:9:1.hebrew: שכל דברי מלכות נחתכין על פיו - לפי תרגום [של] אחשורוש, נענש הרבה שנהרג, דכתיב: "ויגידו למרדכי את דברי אסתר", ולא כתב התם "התך", לפי שהרגו המן על שהיה משיב דברים בין אסתר למרדכי. ומיהו גמ' שלנו אין תופס כן, דדרשינן במגילה (דף טו.): "והתך להיכן הלך", ומפרש: לפי שאין משיבין על הקלקלה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 4a:9:1.english: That all royal matters were decided by his word - According to the Targum of [the book of] Ahasuerus, [Daniel] was punished greatly, in that he was killed. For it is written, "And they told Mordechai the words of Esther," and there it does not write "Hatach," because Haman killed him for relaying messages between Esther and Mordechai. However, our Gemara does not hold this way, for we expound in Megillah (15a): "And Hatach — where did he go?" And it explains: Because one does not relay a reply concerning the ruin [i.e., the evil decree].
